basis: The population is every shipped source family: the nine root modules plus scripts/resolve-repo-pins.py, the three scripts/ci/ files and the three scripts/bench/ files, because all seven scripts run in these workflows, so measuring only the renderers reported coverage for a smaller program than the one that ships. The nine root modules are the post-split set from PR #92 (issue #90): ghwidgets_common.py → ghwidgets_cache.py + ghwidgets_journal.py, and impact_loc.py → impact_clone.py, took the measured population from 13 files to 16, and this record is the deliberate re-measurement over that set — the population-moved refusal (exit 2 on 'Compute the candidate floor') is the tripwire working as designed, not a defect. The floor is the LOWER of the two cells that will read this tree, not this box's number: the ubuntu-latest/3.13 cell has measured three lines differently on impact_loc.py (70 missed there against 67 here), which moves this 3457-statement ratio by 0.087 points, so this box (3.13.14) reads 83.7 and the runner is derived to read 83.6. Pinning the floor to 83.6 rather than 83.7 is what lets the first push to main pass — a floor above the runner's own reading is a red nothing in this repository can lower — and that first raise then re-pins the floor to whatever the runner actually measures, which is the only figure here that was ever a real measurement of the cell the ratchet is calibrated to. The 83.6 is therefore derived from one observed 3-line difference, not measured; if the runner's difference is larger on a given run the first push is red, loudly, and a human re-derives it. The ratchet only ever tightens and this record is no exception: 83.6 sits above the 75.6 it replaces even though the denominator moved 2910 → 3457, because the split modules arrived with their tests. Re-derive the floor, never carry it: the denominator moves whenever a renderer does, and a floor carried across a rebase measures a tree that no longer exists. The record has now moved 12 → 13 (aggregate_gates.py arriving with a rebase) and 13 → 16 (this split) rather than silently comparing a measurement against a floor whose population no longer matches; `raise` refuses outright when the measured file count differs from the `files` recorded here, because a percentage cannot announce that its own denominator changed. The same rebases can also change shipped renderers WITHOUT changing that count — ghwidgets_common.py once went from 376 statements and 51 missed to 369 and 40 — which is the case the file count cannot see, and it is why the numbers above are re-derived rather than carried: a same-population coverage change moves the number silently, and only a person re-deriving it catches that.
